scenes.heading: Specializing: choosing a lane within video

sents.d: Specializing: choosing a lane within video
Weddings, corporate, music videos, and real estate are different businesses that happen to share a camera.

Video work spans wildly different client types, sales cycles, and skills — a wedding client buys emotion and reliability on one irreplaceable day, while a corporate client buys polish, turnaround speed, and professionalism on a recurring basis.
Trying to market to both with the same portfolio and pitch usually undersells you to each.

scenes.heading: A lane makes your message clear

sents.d: Picking a lane doesn't mean permanently ruling anything out — it means your portfolio, pricing, and marketing message speak clearly to one type of buyer instead of vaguely to everyone, which is what actually gets inquiries.

If you're not sure which lane fits, look at which of your past projects you enjoyed most and got the best client reactions on — that's usually a stronger signal than what seems most profitable on paper.

take: Pick one type of client and speak clearly to them.
